Subject: Initial feasibility: minimal private pilot (resource + arch questions)

Team —

Triton Health (cc: Alice) is interested in a very small private (VPC) pilot of Redwood for an internal inference service. They want a narrow scope: single-model endpoint, private control plane, and isolated VPC peering to their AWS account. Before I commit to a timeline I need quick alignment on architecture constraints and a realistic resource ask so I can share an MoS with the customer.

Key asks (please respond inline):
- Minimal infra architecture: what's the smallest valid deployment footprint (GPU class, node count, networking) that keeps 100ms p50 for 512 token requests?
- Security/compliance gates: what evidence will Triton need for KMS/HSM and audit logs for a pilot?
- Operational staffing for a 3-month pilot: onboarding, oncall, SRE support, and an ops runbook.
- Any exception lanes required from product (e.g., disable autoscaling, reduced telemetry retention) to make the pilot viable.

Attached: pilot_sow_draft.docx (draft SOW), ops_headcount_table.xlsx (rough staffing table).

Target: I'd like to give Triton a go/no-go and a resource estimate by EOD Monday. If we need to escalate to Product or Security for an exception, flag that now.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Karthik — good framing. Quick notes from Security/Compliance perspective: 

- KMS/HSM: Triton will need proof of integration with our KMS flow (customer-provided key support) and a written statement about key usage during the pilot. We can provide a one-page integration checklist.
- Audit logs: pilot must include request-level audit logs retained for at least 30 days; if Triton asks for longer retention, that's an exception and will hit storage/ops costs.
- Network: VPC peering + AWS flow logs + strict SG rules are required. We will not allow inbound SSH to any customer-managed nodes.
- SOC2 artifacts: we can share the SOC2 summary and a limited Evidence Request Packet (ERP) tailored for pilots; full evidence takes ~3 weeks to assemble.

Exceptions likely needed:
- Telemetry reduction: if Triton wants to disable or heavily sample logs, that must be approved; recommend we allow sampling but keep SRE traces for regressions.
- Metrics retention beyond 90 days: product/legal approval required.

I'll add a short checklist and upload to the Drive link you listed. If this is going into procurement, we should flag the 3-week ERP timeline to the buyer.

-Kim
Director, Product Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks — putting a concise ops-first estimate here based on similar pilots we've run. I reviewed the attachments. TL;DR: viable, but non-trivial ops cost.

Minimum recommended pilot footprint (to meet ~100ms p50 for 512 tokens):
- 1 x A10G (or equivalent) GPU node for the model runner + 1 small CPU control-plane instance. If Triton accepts a 150ms p50 we can try 1xT4.
- Persistent KV-cache on a small NVMe instance; KMS integration at control plane level only.
- Network: private VPC peering, NAT for egress, hardened SGs.

Staffing (3-month pilot, approximate FTEs):
- Solutions/Onboarding PM: 0.25 FTE (coordination, runbooks, customer sync)
- Infra engineer (deployment + networking): 1.0 FTE for first 6 weeks, then 0.25 FTE for steady ops
- Runtime/SRE engineer: 0.5 FTE (includes oncall rotation, 2-week ramp)
- Security/compliance liaison: to support ERP and evidence — 0.1 FTE (Kim will own most of this formally)
- Support/CS touchpoints: 0.1 FTE

Operational asks from Product/Platform: 
- A temporary exception to allow sampling of telemetry (reduce retention to 30 days) for pilot to limit storage cost. Security flagged this as an exception but recommended sampling as a compromise.
- A one-off control-plane configuration that pins the model and disables autoscaling (we need Product approval; code path exists but not in the standard self-serve).

Risks & mitigations:
- If Triton requires sustained higher throughput, 1 GPU node will saturate; mitigation is a staged scale plan with a clear cost estimate.
- Oncall burden in week 1 is front-loaded; recommend scheduled war room for first 10 business days.

Deliverables I can own if we agree: runbook, onboarding checklist, and a short post-mortem template. I also updated ops_headcount_table.xlsx with the numbers above.

Soojin
Manager, Cloud Operations
Redwood Inference

Karthik / team —

Thanks for the quick responses and the level of detail. Triton remains interested in the narrow pilot as described. A couple of clarifications from our side: 
- We can accept 150ms p50 in exchange for lower cost while we validate model outputs for a single internal workflow (clinical QA).
- We can live with 30-day logs for the pilot; longer retention will be considered later.
- Preferred go-live: no earlier than 2027-06-15 to align with our security review cycle.

Next steps from Triton: I will share our network connectivity diagram and a PO contact by Monday. We may ask for a one-time discount on the pilot seat rates (procurement request) — I will surface that once I have internal approvals.

If you can confirm the staffing estimate and the single-GPU option (T4 acceptable with 150ms goal), we'll move forward with the SOW as-is and get procurement in motion.

Best,
Alice Park
Director, Data Platform
Triton Health
